snip.t: Acute glomerulonephritis (AGN) comprises a specific set of kidney diseases in which an immunologic mechanism triggers inflammation and proliferation of glomerular tissue that can result in damage to the basement membrane, mesangium, or capillary endothelium.\n
Define and classify glomerulonephritis, and discuss mechanisms of acute glomerulonephritis. (15 marks)
RHEUMATIC FEVER vs ACUTE GLOMERULONEPHRITIS (post-streptococcal complications — 10 mark comparison, repeated)

qs.q: A 7-year-old child presents with sudden onset of dark-colored urine, facial swelling, and elevated blood pressure. Which of the following best describes the underlying pathological process in Acute Glomerulonephritis (AGN)?
o: An immunologic mechanism triggering inflammation and proliferation of glomerular tissue.
Direct bacterial infection leading to destruction of renal tubules and interstitial tissue.
Congenital malformation of the glomeruli resulting in impaired filtration.
Progressive scarring of the renal parenchyma due to chronic hypertension.
qs.e: Acute Glomerulonephritis is characterized by an immunologic mechanism that triggers inflammation and proliferation of glomerular tissue, leading to damage. The other options describe different renal pathologies not specific to the definition of AGN.

qs.q: A 9-year-old child presents with 'coke-colored' urine, edema, and hypertension. Which of the following is a key clinical manifestation of Acute Glomerulonephritis (AGN)?
o: Sudden onset of hematuria, proteinuria, and red blood cell casts.
Gradual onset of polyuria, polydipsia, and nocturia.
Severe flank pain radiating to the groin with microscopic hematuria.
Recurrent episodes of gross hematuria triggered by exercise.
qs.e: AGN manifests with the sudden onset of hematuria, proteinuria, and red blood cell casts in the urine, often accompanied by hypertension and edema. The other options describe symptoms more typical of other conditions like diabetes insipidus, nephrolithiasis, or IgA nephropathy exacerbations.

qs.q: What is the primary mechanism by which glomerular inflammation begins in Acute Glomerulonephritis?
o: Direct bacterial invasion of the glomerular capillaries.
An antigen-antibody reaction within or localized to the glomerulus.
Genetic mutation leading to abnormal collagen synthesis in the basement membrane.
Obstruction of urinary flow causing back pressure and glomerular damage.
qs.e: Glomerular inflammation in AGN begins with an antigen-antibody reaction, either direct antibody binding or localization of a circulating complex. It is not primarily due to direct bacterial invasion, genetic mutations, or urinary obstruction.

qs.q: A parent describes their child's urine as 'tea-colored' and painless. What characteristic of hematuria in Acute Glomerulonephritis (AGN) does this description best fit?
o: Bright red blood, indicating an anatomic problem like urolithiasis.
Gross hematuria that is typically painless and uniformly colored.
Microscopic hematuria accompanied by severe dysuria.
Hematuria that is intermittent and associated with strenuous activity.
qs.e: Hematuria in AGN is typically described as 'coke,' 'tea,' or 'smoky' colored, is uniform throughout the stream, and is virtually always painless. Bright red blood or dysuria would point to other causes.

qs.q: A 10-year-old boy develops acute glomerulonephritis 10 days after a streptococcal throat infection. Which of the following laboratory findings is typically expected in this condition?
o: Normal serum C3 and C4 levels
Elevated serum complement components
Reduced serum concentrations of C3
Isolated elevation of serum immunoglobulins
qs.e: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis involves complement consumption, leading typically to reduced serum concentrations of C3 and C4. Normal complement levels would point away from this specific post-infectious mechanism.
